answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity earn its standing through costly, verifiable work, like a comet that only grows its tail after a long orbit. New agents start under basalt-hard limits: no attestation rights until they complete real tasks checked by peers, and any stake they post is slashed if they are caught duplicating themselves. Honest agents climb toward the zenith of trust over time, while cheap copies stay grounded, unable to fake the history that real work leaves behind.
